items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: I said in my day if you were at all interested in music you could not equivocate. For example, you had to either be for Benny Goodman or for Artie Shaw.

ctx.x: I come from a totally non-musical family background. I remember quite distinctly that when I was about six a relative was breaking up a household and had a piano that she was willing to give to us and my mother said if we have a piano in the house, will you take lessons, which was a pretty stupid question for my mother to ask me, and I said hell no, or whatever a 6-year-old said, the equivalent of that, to my mother. And so I grew up quite non-musical. But what you have to remember is that when I was growing up…

Benny Goodman or for Artie Shaw. You couldn’t waffle on that. And Artie, among other things has a wonderful sense of humor but not about himself. His response to that was to tell me quite seriously, “well Benny was a better clarinet player, but I was a better musician.” But at any rate you listened to a lot of that. You listened to a lot of Ellington. I mean I think the Ellington band was one of the first musics that I was conscious of. And then of course the other strange thing was I was going to clubs and…
